title: Will the launch spike last?
hook: Compare an early window with a later window under an explicit decay rule.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: a new design spikes clicks for a week, then fades back.

misconception: Treating novelty effect as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: a new design spikes clicks for a week, then fades back.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: A stipulated daily lift follows L(t)=2+18 exp(−t/3), in percentage points. What lift remains on day 9?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-novelty-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Daily lift model L(t)=2+18 exp(-t/3), in percentage points. Day0=20, day3≈8.622, day9≈2.896. Compare early-only reading with late sustained effect2.

src/demos/probability/p100-novelty-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Daily lift model L(t)=2+18 exp(-t/3), in percentage points. Day0=20, day3≈8.622, day9≈2.896. Compare early-only reading with late sustained effect2.

claims.text: The late window retains 2.896 points on day 9; the early window retains 20 on day 0. The model’s temporary term decays while its sustained term stays at 2.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-novelty-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Daily lift model L(t)=2+18 exp(-t/3), in percentage points. Day0=20, day3≈8.622, day9≈2.896. Compare early-only reading with late sustained effect2.

claims.text: A launch-window average would blend those components. This is an explicit hypothetical decay rule, not evidence that real product gains always fade or that day 9 is enough for every experiment.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-novelty-effect/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Daily lift model L(t)=2+18 exp(-t/3), in percentage points. Day0=20, day3≈8.622, day9≈2.896. Compare early-only reading with late sustained effect2.

claims.text: In L(t)=3+12 exp(−t/2), which term survives as t grows? The exponential term tends to zero, leaving the stipulated sustained component 3.
